title: Opposite-Color Paintbrush
normalExpectation: Brush applies paint color loaded on it.
response: Whatever color you load, the brush deposits the complementary color; loading blue paints orange, loading red paints green.
whyThisObject: Brush is a transfer tool for pigment; if it inverts color, painting a chosen color is impossible.
trigger: Mimi strokes blue paint; wall turns orange.
goalInterference: The action to apply blue paint produces orange, so the wall never becomes blue.
frameZero: Mimi stands at a wall with a blue paint bucket and brush mid-stroke; the painted patch is vivid orange.

sourceBeats.strategy: Mimi mixes a custom color equal parts blue and orange, hoping inversion cancels.
sourceBeats.visibleConsequence: The brush paints a shimmering gray that immediately splits into blue and orange stripes.
sourceBeats.newInformation: Complementary inversion doesn't cancel but separates into two colors.

sourceBeats.strategy: Mimi tries to paint the wall orange, expecting inversion to give blue.
sourceBeats.visibleConsequence: The wall turns blue-green, not pure blue, and the brush swirls automatically.
sourceBeats.newInformation: The inversion rule includes a hue shift, so aiming for orange doesn't yield blue.

sourceBeats.strategy: Mimi uses a roller instead of brush.
sourceBeats.visibleConsequence: The roller paints the opposite color at triple scale, covering the wall in a giant orange sunburst.
sourceBeats.newInformation: The inversion applies to any painting tool, increasing area.

sourceBeats.strategy: Mimi puts a stencil on the wall to paint a pattern.
sourceBeats.visibleConsequence: The stencil areas stay original color, while the exposed wall turns complementary, creating a negative of the pattern.
sourceBeats.newInformation: The brush inverts color in the open areas, not just strokes.

sourceBeats.strategy: Mimi gives up and paints the wall back white.
sourceBeats.visibleConsequence: The white paint turns black, then the entire wall flashes and becomes a mirror reflecting the room in inverted colors.
sourceBeats.newInformation: Painting white triggers a full-wall color inversion, turning the wall into a funhouse mirror.
